messages:
incident-bot: PagerDuty alert fired -> redis-prod cluster: maxclients reached, connections refused. Severity: P1. PD:PD-98765. paging eng-oncall.

pagerduty: PagerDuty: Incident PD-98765 routed to group eng-oncall; escalation timer started.

maria-b: ack. oncall here, pulling metrics.

kevin: ping — saw some 5xx spikes from frontend graphs around the same time.

maria-b: confirmed — frontend 5xxs and 200ms->1.2s tail latency. Errors are Redis connection refused when trying to read session cache.

ashley: any known deploys? I see no deploys in last 30m.

maria-b: no deploys. checking redis INFO and slowlog. running: `redis-cli -h redis-prod-1 info clients | grep connected_clients`

maria-b: snippet from host: `connected_clients:10240` — server reports at maxclients (10k). `maxclients:10000`. lots of TIME_WAIT sockets.

ops-bot: Alert from monitoring: redis-prod-1 latency spike, evictions, and ERR max number of clients reached.

kevin: could be a connection leak from a background job or new batch job. any batch jobs starting at :00?

maria-b: searching. Found a nightly ingestion job started a minute before the spike on prod-workers that streams to Redis sets. PID list shows many long-lived tcp connections from worker pods.

ashley: can we throttle that ingestion or pause it? It writes to a set with `SADD` bursts. If we pause, cache reads should recover.

maria-b: agreed. issuing a graceful pause: `kubectl -n prod scale deployment ingestion-workers --replicas=0` to stop starting new tasks; will drain current ones with SIGTERM.

maria-b: command run. now checking connections.

incident-bot: Deployment ingestion-workers scaled to 0 replicas.

maria-b: connections down to ~5400 — getting better. frontend errors dropping.

kevin: nice. what's the plan for long term? 10k maxclients seems low for current traffic.

ashley: yes we also saw connection storms from many short-lived client connections. Are apps using connection pooling?

maria-b: looks like some older services open a new redis socket per request (legacy lib). I have a list: session-service, analytics-proxy, ingestion-workers (now paused). We'll queue tech debt P0 to migrate to pooled clients or reuse.

sre-lead: short-term options: (1) increase `maxclients` on Redis (requires rolling restart, risk of memory/FD exhaustion), (2) enforce connection pooling on app side, (3) scale Redis horizontally to add shards/replicas, or (4) apply iptable conn tracking tweaks to reduce TIME_WAIT.

maria-b: quick mitigation: restarted a handful of leaking pods that held sockets open: `kubectl -n prod delete pod session-auth-7d9f` and rolled the session-service deployment. Also enabled sticky connection pooling on session-service temporarily (env var flip).

kevin: after restarts + ingestion pause, metrics show connected_clients ~2200 and stable. 5xxs mostly resolved.

ashley: customer impact? any premium customers seeing errors?

maria-b: checked logs — spike produced ~2.4% error rate for 6 minutes. A small subset of user requests got 503 when session lookup failed. No data loss. Posting to status: `Partial degraded performance for session lookups — transient 503s for ~6m`

maria-b: created incident channel `#inc-redis-1795523001` and incident doc in runbook with initial timeline and mitigation steps.

sre-lead: good. action items: 1) ops to schedule controlled increase of `maxclients` by 25% with monitoring and a rolling restart in maintenance window; 2) dev teams to adopt connection pooling; 3) add alerts to detect sudden connection growth patterns (delta threshold).

maria-b: assigning tasks: @ashley to coordinate app changes (session-service + analytics-proxy). @kevin to own infra followup (maxclients + capacity planning). I'll handoff to @kevin after I finish postmortem notes.

kevin: ack. I'll monitor for next 30m and take over on-call. please add any logs to the incident doc.

maria-b: leaving for handoff — last check: redis connected_clients 2300, no new error spikes, frontend 5xx <0.1%. PD incident still open until we close after postmortem.

kevin: I'll keep watch. if anything flares, escalate to SRE-lead.

incident-bot: PagerDuty PD-98765 updated: acknowledged by maria-b, ownership transferred to kevin.

maria-b: closing thread here for now; continuing documentation in incident channel. thanks team :thumbsup:

kevin: thanks — will follow up with a timeline and RCA draft.
